2608.21721.title: Ask or Answer: A Decision Framework for Multi-Turn Health Misinformation Intervention
2608.21721.paper_summary: Correcting health misinformation in dialogue requires more than producing a factual rebuttal: users differ in what they know, what they believe, and what they need to hear, so an effective intervention often depends on first asking the right clarifying question. Yet existing methods either respond immediately or probe indiscriminately, treating clarification as either unnecessary or always beneficial. We propose Reward-Optimized Probe-and-Respond (RO-PnR), a framework that learns when asking is worth its cost. At each turn, RO-PnR chooses between probing for more information and committing to a final correction, guided by a turn-level reward that weighs the expected gain from probing against its interaction cost. To capture how user heterogeneity affects probing value, we model each simulated user with a latent state along health literacy and belief commitment. Experiments show that RO-PnR achieves the highest cost-adjusted utility across three health-misinformation datasets and three base models, using 30% fewer turns than always-probe baselines.
2608.21721.paper_summary_zh: 糾正對話中的健康錯誤資訊不僅僅需要提供事實上的反駁：用戶在他們所知道的、所相信的和需要聽到的內容上各有不同，因此有效的干預往往依賴於首先提出正確的澄清問題。然而，現有的方法要麼立即回應，要麼無差別地探詢，將澄清視為不必要或總是有益。我們提出了獎勵優化探詢與回應（RO-PnR）框架，該框架學習在何時詢問是值得其成本的。在每一回合中，RO-PnR 在探詢更多信息和承諾最終修正之間進行選擇，這是由一個回合級別的獎勵指導的，該獎勵權衡了探詢的預期收益與其互動成本。為了捕捉用戶異質性如何影響探詢價值，我們將每個模擬用戶建模為在健康素養和信念承諾上的潛在狀態。實驗顯示，RO-PnR 在三個健康錯誤資訊數據集和三個基礎模型中實現了最高的成本調整效用，使用的回合數比始終探詢的基準少30%。
